cards.text: Friend, meet Isaiah the prophet. The LORD has just told him that the king of Assyria will sweep over Judah like a flood (Isaiah 8:7-8). Now the LORD speaks to Isaiah with a strong hand and tells him not to walk in the way of this people.
The LORD says not to call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy, and I picture a 2 a.m. group chat with FORTY-SEVEN unread messages that all start with "Did you hear?!"

cards.question: The LORD tells Isaiah not to call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy. What else does He tell him?

answers.text: Do not fear what they fear
Warn them to fear it more

cards.question: Isaiah isn't supposed to fear what these people fear. So who is the only one he should fear?

cards.text: The LORD will be a sanctuary. But the LORD says there's another side to that for both houses of Israel and for the people of Jerusalem.

cards.question: To both houses of Israel, the LORD will be a stone of stumbling.

cards.text: Many will stumble over these, fall and be broken, ensnared and captured. Then comes a command to wrap something up tight, the way I tape my cookie boxes so good even I can't get back in: 'Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.'

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. What does Isaiah say he will do?

answers.text: Wait for the LORD and trust Him
Look for help from another god

cards.text: Then Isaiah says, 'Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me…' I bet he's proud of them, and as the papa of six cookie cutter kids, I get it, because some bakers have heard about my kids THREE TIMES in one visit.

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD gave him his children as signs and symbols in Israel.

cards.text: Then Isaiah brings up a moment when men say to consult mediums and spiritists, the ones who whisper and mutter.

cards.question: When men say to consult mediums, Isaiah asks: shouldn't a people consult their ___ instead?
Isaiah has one more question about the mediums: why consult the ___ on behalf of the living?

cards.text: Then the call goes out, loud and clear: 'To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no light of dawn.'
This part is heavy, friend. Isaiah says people will roam the land, dejected and hungry.

cards.question: Isaiah says people will roam the land, dejected and hungry, and when they are famished they will become enraged. Looking upward, what will they do?

answers.text: Curse their king and their God
Cry out to God for mercy

cards.question: When the hungry, enraged people roaming the land look to the earth, they will finally see the light of dawn.

cards.text: Those people will see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish, and they will be driven into utter darkness. Hold on to that picture, friend.
Then Isaiah says one word that turns everything around: NEVERTHELESS. There will be no more gloom for those in distress, and friend, I want that word stitched on my apron.

cards.question: Isaiah says that in the future God will honor Galilee of the nations. Which two lands does he say God humbled in the past?

cards.text: Now picture the people walking in darkness, living in the land of the shadow of death.

cards.question: The people walking in darkness have seen a great ___.

cards.text: On them, a light has dawned, and friend, I KNOW that feeling. In the junk drawer where I spent years, that slice of kitchen light was everything, and even the dead batteries I shared it with sat up straight with ZERO charge to sit up with.

cards.question: God has enlarged the nation and increased its joy. The people rejoice before Him the way people rejoice at what?

cards.text: Isaiah points back to the day of Midian, a nation that once had the upper hand over Israel for seven years (Judges 6:1-2). Something has been broken, and this time it's not the people.

cards.question: As in the day of Midian, God has shattered the rod of their oppressor.
Isaiah mentions every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood. What will happen to them?

answers.text: Burned as fuel for the fire
Stored up for the next war

cards.text: 'For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given…' Isaiah says, and friend, THIS is the moment the whole passage has been building to.

cards.question: God broke the bar across the people's shoulders. Now the government will be upon whose shoulders?

cards.text: Isaiah says, 'And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.' Friend, I could sit with that line all day.

cards.question: Isaiah says the child's government and peace will keep increasing with no end.

cards.text: This child will reign on the throne of David, Israel's king, and over his kingdom.

cards.question: The child will establish and sustain David's kingdom with justice and ___ from that time and forevermore.
Isaiah says the people's own efforts will accomplish the child's reign on David's throne.

cards.text: 'The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.' Not the people, not an army, and definitely not me and my mustache, and friend, I am SO glad about that last one.
